_comment: Tier-2 for skfem hyperelasticity#5, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: the geometric term S : grad(du)^T grad(v) is essential; dropping it gives quadratic convergence at small strains (<5%) but STAGNATES at large strains, dropping ~10x then flat-lining around 1e-6 absolute. Ran: total-Lagrangian PK2 Neo-Hookean, MeshTri().refined(3), ElementVector(ElementTriP1), 162 DOFs, mu=lam=1, exact tangent vs material-only tangent at 2% and 30% right-edge stretch. Printed: 'QUADRATIC AT SMALL STRAINS' IS FALSE -- at 2% stretch (inside the claim's own <5% window) the material-only tangent converges LINEARLY at a constant ratio of 0.052, taking 8 iterations against the exact tangent's 3; it still reaches the right answer, so only the rate reveals the bug. At 30% stretch the shape of the claim holds: the residual drops 8.76x, flat-lines within a factor 1.113 over five iterations, and then goes NaN -- worse than stagnation. THE PLATEAU LEVEL IS WRONG: it sits at 1.77e-03, not 'around 1e-6', so the absolute threshold in the entry is unusable and the history SHAPE (drop then flat) is the real signal.
